brief:
More than seventy years after displacement, Palestinians scattered across the world continue bearing witness to their homeland, Shehab Wire reported. Those who left Palestine after the 1948 Nakba carried keys to homes they never returned to and memories of villages etched in collective memory. Successive generations born in exile have inherited this connection to a place most have never lived.

The diaspora's relationship to Palestine persists as lived experience rather than inherited rhetoric, passed down through families and communities that refuse forgetting.

title: Palestinians in diaspora carry homeland across seven decades
